sections.title: Advanced Functional Equations
sections.content: Identify standard functions based on equations. If f(x+y) = f(x)f(y), f(x) = a^x. If f(xy) = f(x)+f(y), f(x) = log(x). If f(x)f(1/x) = f(x)+f(1/x), f(x) = ±x^n + 1. Use differentiation (keeping one variable constant) to solve complex ones.

sections.title: Limits using Series Expansions
sections.content: For complex 0/0 limits where L'Hopital is too tedious, use Maclaurin series. e^x = 1 + x + x²/2! + ... ; sin x = x - x³/3! + ... ; cos x = 1 - x²/2! + ... ; ln(1+x) = x - x²/2 + x³/3 - ...

sections.title: Analyzing Points of Non-Differentiability
sections.content: Functions involving absolute values (modulus), greatest integer [x], or fractional part {x} are prime candidates. Modulus |f(x)| is non-differentiable where f(x)=0 AND f'(x)≠0 (sharp corners on x-axis).

sections.title: Higher-Order Derivatives & Leibnitz Theorem
sections.content: Leibnitz theorem finds the nth derivative of a product: (uv)_n = nC0 u_n v + nC1 u_{n-1} v_1 + ... + nCn u v_n. Useful when one function's derivatives vanish quickly (like polynomials).

sections.title: Maxima, Minima & Global Extrema
sections.content: First Derivative Test gives local extrema. Second Derivative Test: f''(x) < 0 (Local Max), f''(x) > 0 (Local Min). Global extrema in [a,b] are found by checking values at all critical points AND the endpoints a and b.

sections.title: Rolle's Theorem & Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem (LMVT)
sections.content: Rolle's: If f(x) is continuous in [a,b], differentiable in (a,b), and f(a)=f(b), there exists at least one c in (a,b) where f'(c)=0. LMVT: Under same conditions (without f(a)=f(b)), f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a).

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Applying LMVT or Rolle's without checking if the function is non-differentiable at even a single point in the interval (e.g., |x| in [-1,1]).
2) Stopping the series expansion too early when terms cancel out in limit evaluation.
3) Missing boundary points when finding Global Max/Min.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 tackles JEE Advanced concepts: recognizing functional equations, bypassing limits with infinite series, identifying non-differentiable kinks, and proving root existence using LMVT.

tricks.title: Newton-Leibnitz Rule (Differentiating Integrals)
tricks.explanation: d/dx [ ∫(from a(x) to b(x)) f(t) dt ] = f(b(x))*b'(x) - f(a(x))*a'(x). Crucial for limits involving definite integrals.
tricks.example: d/dx ∫(0 to x²) e^t dt = e^(x²) * 2x - 0.

tricks.title: Differentiability of Max/Min Functions
tricks.explanation: For h(x) = max(f(x), g(x)), the points of non-differentiability strictly occur at the intersection points where f(x) = g(x) (provided their slopes are unequal there).
tricks.example: max(x, x²) is non-differentiable at x=0 and x=1.

tricks.title: Optimization in Geometry Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Max area of a rectangle inscribed in a circle of radius R is a square of area 2R². Max volume of a cylinder in a sphere is when height = 2R/√3.
tricks.example: Saves heavy calculus derivation during exams.

tricks.title: LMVT Root Existence Trick
tricks.explanation: To prove an equation f(x)=0 has a root in (a,b), construct an integral function F(x) = ∫f(x)dx. Show F(a) = F(b). By Rolle's theorem, F'(x) = f(x) = 0 has a root in (a,b).
tricks.example: Proving ax²+bx+c=0 has a root in (0,1) if a/3 + b/2 + c = 0.

tricks.title: Corner Points in Nested Modulus
tricks.explanation: For f(x) = ||x-a|-b|, critical points are at x=a, x=a+b, x=a-b. Check the slope at these exact points to count non-differentiability points.

tricks.title: Series Expansion Degree Check
tricks.explanation: When using series expansion for limits of form f(x)/x^n as x->0, the limit is finite and non-zero ONLY if the lowest power of x in the numerator expansion is exactly n.
tricks.example: Use this to quickly find unknown coefficients a, b in limit problems by equating lower degree coefficients to 0.
